intents.name: internship_info
intents.answer:
An internship is a short, structured work experience (usually 1–6 months) where a student works with an organisation to learn real skills.

Why it helps:
• Practical experience beyond classroom theory
• A stronger resume and portfolio
• Industry contacts and mentors
• A route to pre-placement offers and full-time jobs
suggestions: Which internship is best for me?

intents.name: eligibility
intents.answer:
Eligibility depends on the company or program, but commonly:
• Currently enrolled in a degree or diploma course (often B.Tech/BCA/MCA/BSc and similar)
• Usually 2nd year onwards, though some programs accept 1st year
• Relevant basic skills for the role
• Some programs set a minimum CGPA or percentage

⚠️ Exact criteria differ for each program. Always check the official listing or ask your internship coordinator.

intents.name: application_process
intents.answer:
Typical steps to apply:
1. Find a suitable internship on the official portal, college placement cell or company careers page
2. Check eligibility and the deadline
3. Prepare your resume (and cover letter if asked)
4. Fill in the online application form
5. Upload the required documents
6. Submit and note your application ID
7. Prepare for a test or interview if shortlisted

Apply early, because deadlines are usually strict.

intents.name: required_documents
intents.answer:
Commonly required documents:
• Updated resume / CV
• College ID card or bonafide certificate
• Latest marksheet or academic records
• Photo ID (e.g. Aadhaar)
• Passport-size photograph
• NOC / permission letter from college (if required)
• Portfolio, GitHub link or project details (for technical roles)

The exact list is set by each program, so confirm it in the official notice.
suggestions: How to write a good resume?

intents.name: duration
intents.answer:
Internship duration varies by program:
• Short-term / winter: 2–4 weeks
• Summer internships: 6–8 weeks
• Standard internships: 2–6 months
• Long-term or semester-long: 6 months

The exact start date, end date and weekly hours are given in the offer letter.

intents.name: stipend
intents.answer:
It depends on the program:
• Paid internships offer a monthly stipend (amount varies by company, role and city)
• Unpaid internships give experience, mentoring and a certificate but no money
• Some give a performance-based stipend or a pre-placement offer

The stipend is always stated in the official listing or offer letter. I don't want to guess an amount for you.

intents.name: fees
intents.answer:
Genuine company internships do not normally charge students. Some training-based programs charge a course fee, and that should be clearly described.

⚠️ Be careful: if someone asks for money to 'guarantee' an internship, verify the organisation first. Check the company website, reviews and your college placement cell before paying anything.

intents.name: application_status
patterns: how do i check my application status
intents.answer:
To check your application status:
• Log in to the portal where you applied and open 'My Applications'
• Check your email (including spam) for updates
• Contact the internship coordinator with your application ID

I can't see individual student records, so please use the official portal for personal status.

intents.name: selection_process
intents.answer:
A typical selection process:
1. Resume screening
2. Online test or assignment (aptitude / technical)
3. Technical or HR interview
4. Offer letter

Interview tips:
• Know every project on your resume in depth
• Revise core basics of your field
• Be ready to explain why you want this role
• Keep a short list of questions to ask them
suggestions: How to write a good resume?

intents.name: certificate
intents.answer:
Most internships issue a completion certificate once you finish the program successfully.

Common conditions:
• Complete the full duration
• Submit assigned tasks, projects or reports
• Meet attendance / performance requirements

Some companies also give a letter of recommendation or an experience letter for strong performers. Check the program guidelines for specifics.

intents.name: best_internship

• Web Development: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React, Flask or Node
• Data Science / Analytics: Python, SQL, statistics, visualisation
• AI / Machine Learning: Python, ML basics, projects

intents.name: resume
patterns: how to write a good resume
intents.answer:
A strong internship resume:
• One page, clean format, no photo unless asked
• Header: name, email, phone, LinkedIn, GitHub
• Education with CGPA / percentage
• Projects with what you built, tools used and the result
• Skills grouped by category
• Achievements, certifications, positions of responsibility

Use action verbs ('Built', 'Designed') and numbers where possible. Proofread twice!

intents.name: application_guide
patterns: how do i prepare for internships
intents.answer:
Complete Step-by-Step Internship Application Guide 📋

**1. Eligibility Check:**
• Open to students enrolled in Bachelor's, Master's, or Diploma degrees (B.Tech, BCA, MCA, BSc, etc.).
• Most tech companies accept 2nd, 3rd, and final year students (early programs like Google STEP accept 1st and 2nd years).
• Maintain a 60%+ or 6.5+ CGPA to satisfy company eligibility filters.

**2. Required Skills:**
• Master one programming language (Python, Java, C++, or JavaScript).
• Strong grasp of Data Structures, Algorithms, and Git/GitHub.
• Build 2–3 end-to-end, functional projects that solve real problems.

**3. Required Documents:**
• Updated 1-page resume (with clickable GitHub & LinkedIn links).
• College ID / Bonafide Certificate and latest academic marksheets.
• Photo ID (Aadhaar / Passport) and NOC from college if required.

**4. Application Steps:**
• Apply directly through official portals: [Google](https://careers.google.com/students/), [Microsoft](https://careers.microsoft.com/students/us/en), [Amazon](https://www.amazon.jobs/content/en/career-programs/student-programs), [IBM](https://www.ibm.com/careers/internships), [Infosys](https://www.infosys.com/careers/entry-level/in-step-internship.html), [TCS](https://www.tcs.com/careers/india/entry-level), or [AICTE](https://internship.aicte-india.org/).
• Submit early (applications often close once interview quotas are reached).
• Save your application tracking ID and check your email regularly.

**5. Selection Process:**
• Resume Screening ➔ Online Coding & Aptitude Test ➔ Technical Round ➔ HR / Behavioral Interview ➔ Offer Letter.

intents.name: resume_checker_faq
intents.answer:
ATS Resume Checker & Optimization 📄

**Key Guidelines for a Recruiter-Ready Resume:**
1. **Quantify Your Impact**: Use measurable numbers (e.g. *'reduced latency by 40%'*, *'served 500+ users'*).
2. **Include Essential Sections**: Education with CGPA, Technical Skills, Key Projects with GitHub links, and Experience.
3. **Targeted Technical Keywords**: Include the exact tech stack (e.g. Java, Spring Boot, MySQL or React, Node.js, MongoDB).
4. **Use Strong Action Verbs**: Begin bullet points with *'Developed'*, *'Architected'*, *'Implemented'*, *'Automated'* rather than passive phrases.
5. **Clean 1-Page Layout**: Keep it strictly one page for college internships.

Use the **Resume Checker** tab in the sidebar to upload your PDF or DOCX resume for an instant ATS score and keyword gap analysis!

intents.name: interview_prep_faq
intents.answer:
Technical Interview Preparation & Practice 🎯

**Effective 4-Step Interview Strategy:**
1. **Revise Core Concepts**: Master language fundamentals, OOP principles, memory models, and database querying.
2. **Solve Topic-Wise MCQs**: Test yourself on edge cases, memory management, and language semantics.
3. **Hands-On Coding Challenges**: Practice common array, string, and hash table algorithm problems.
4. **Simulate Mock Interviews**: Practice explaining your thought process out loud under timed constraints.

Navigate to the **Practice & Mock Interview** section in the sidebar to solve interactive MCQs, view starter coding templates, and run mock interview simulations!
